summary: Root-cause analysis: why the reconstruct silent-defect fix track (PR #97) keeps producing deeper findings each codex round

candidate_roots.root_cause: Reconstruct is a replay/resume-capable pipeline where every stage re-reads artifacts from disk and is therefore forbidden to trust an upstream stage's in-memory guarantee. A given semantic property (a candidate limitation must reach the public claim; this evidence must fit the unsplittable single-question prompt; this material is projected whole) is consequently implemented as a SET of independent, hand-written re-assertions — one in the builder, one in each downstream validator, one in each projection, one in the resume/reuse path — with no single declarative invariant from which all those points are derived. Each Codex fix hardens exactly the one stage the reviewer named, leaving every other member of the same fixed-length chain free to contradict it. The number of review rounds is therefore bounded only by the chain length, not by the correctness of any individual fix: the residual is structurally guaranteed to exist at the next stage.
candidate_roots.mechanism: Verified in code: candidate_limitation_refs is re-checked by three separate near-identical Set blocks at maturation-validation.ts:670-681 (baseline↔candidate), :980-993 (matrix↔baseline), :3911-3934 (continuation actionable_ready + decision.limitation_refs), plus a builder branch at :3720 and a claim projection — five carry-forward surfaces for ONE value. Likewise the 50K prompt cap (run.ts:778) is enforced by three independently-tuned proxies (EVIDENCE_EXCERPT_LIMIT=4_000 :782, EVIDENCE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT=50 :792, EVIDENCE_TOTAL_BUDGET_CHARS=24_000 :789) feeding boundEvidenceBySerializedSize (:4039) and boundSingleEvidenceItem (:4020). The full-excerpt eligibility predicate isFullExcerptProjectionEligible (run.ts:5700) is re-threaded by hand into :5724, :5831, :5882 and forked into materialize-preparation.ts:327-328 (whose comment literally points back to run.ts). Each fix walks one stage further down a fixed chain.
candidate_roots.source_lenses: coupling (hyp 1), enforcement-locus (hyp 15), concept-flow (hyp 11), process-method (hyp 20), input-variation (hyp 25 split-scope)
candidate_roots.finding_coverage: The serial regeneration of all three clusters: #22 candidate_limitation chain (87cd9b8 F2/F4 → 7923f02 R2-2/R2-5 → e88c119 R3-1/R3-2 → c61cc22 R6-3 → R7 final-requestion), #1 evidence-budget chain (86324da → 1f4b2da R4 count-cap → 07dcdef R5 serialized-size → c61cc22 R6 per-item-stub → R7 stub-honesty), #21 truncation chain (a464732 → R2-1/R2-3 capture/resume → R3-3 label → R5-2 e2e). Same invariant, re-enforced one node later each round.

candidate_roots.root_cause: Validators verify that the elements PRESENT in an artifact resolve and are internally consistent, but never reconstruct the EXPECTED/closed set from upstream authority (selected.adequacy_frame.required_elements) and assert conservation/set-equality. This is a distinct failure axis from per-stage mirroring: even after every consistency seam is patched, the omission class (a deleted baseline row, a matrix that drops a baseline row, a claim_scope that omits non-closed rows) remains structurally invisible — so it can silently ERASE blocker/high scope. Each round's fix tightens one more present-record predicate; the reviewer then constructs the dual (delete the record), which passes every present-record guard.
candidate_roots.mechanism: Verified: maturation-validation.ts:652 builds the expected element map from required_elements, but :709 only checks baseline_rows.length===0 and :716 iterates `for (const row of baseline.baseline_rows)` — validating present rows only, never diffing against the derived expected tuple set. :1003 iterates matrix.rows without requiring one row per baseline row. No grep hit for an expected-tuple-set-and-diff anywhere in the validator. The per-round additions are all Set membership/equality checks bolted on per-field, not a generic derive-expected-set-and-compare.
candidate_roots.finding_coverage: Explains why the CLI adversarial P1 trio is the ONLY high-severity set still completely unaddressed across all 7 rounds: maturation-validation.ts:716 (deleting any required row passes, can erase blocker scope), :1003 (matrix not 1:1 with baseline), :3885 (claim_scope omits non-closed rows → claim projection preserves the lie). These require deriving completeness from required_elements, which no round attempted — sharpening why the loop never converges on the load-bearing integrity gaps.

candidate_roots.root_cause: Runtime code is treated as the sole authority and the declared-capability surfaces — the reconstruct-contract-registry obligations, the .onto seeding/maturation design doc, the internal concept type names, and the reuse/projection contract sha — are reconciled AFTER the fact rather than derived from or drift-tested against the runtime. So every new concept (candidate_limitation_refs, source_evidence_projection, evidence_body_omitted_for_budget, the code-widened truncation label) is born wired-but-undeclared. Fixtures or resume artifacts built from the documented shape, or reused pre-change artifacts, then pass against validators/contracts that don't yet know the field, regenerating a desync finding every round until each surface is hand-synced.
candidate_roots.mechanism: Verified: grep of reconstruct-contract-registry.yaml returns ZERO matches for candidate_limitation_refs, source_evidence_projection, or evidence_body_omitted across all 9 commits — the rank-5 feature-contract authority was never touched, while runtime added three validators and new prompt-contract fields. git diff shows ontology-seeding-and-maturation-design.md (+14) and artifact-types.ts (+8) were catch-up syncs landed AFTER the runtime validators already dereferenced the field. The projection-contract sha was bumped reactively v2→v3→v4 round by round (run.ts ~768) rather than derived once. The DocumentExcerptProjectionTruncation type name stayed document-scoped after its meaning widened to code.
candidate_roots.finding_coverage: The contract-sync cluster: F1/R2-6 reuse-hash non-rotation, R5-3 + artifact-types.ts:1933 .onto omitted required field, and all four CLI concept-perspective findings (registry:2545 obligations don't declare match/carry-forward/claim-limitation rules; run.ts:807 source_evidence_projection owned by no .onto shape; run.ts:5568 DocumentExcerptProjectionTruncation still document-scoped; run.ts:4286 Unresolved Revision Proposals section not in deterministic_runtime_append_sections).

candidate_roots.root_cause: Per-material-kind behavior (capture budget, whole-text projection eligibility, evidence sizing, truncation provenance, AND security/consumption posture) is encoded as scattered inline kind=='document'/kind=='code' branches across many runtime sites rather than behind one per-kind policy object. The closed kind enum exists, but each behavioral rule has no single owner, so widening eligibility for one kind (document→code→config) must be re-applied at each site or that site silently disagrees — and crucially the projection surface grew faster than the authorization gate, so widening 'code' to whole-file capture turned into a data-exposure hole when the classifier maps .env/secret-bearing config to 'code' while source-safety still marks prompt-context refs consumption_allowed.
candidate_roots.mechanism: Verified: isFullExcerptProjectionEligible (run.ts:5700, document-text-readable OR code) is re-threaded into :5724, :5831, :5882 and re-stated as a parallel predicate in materialize-preparation.ts:327-328 (kind==='code' || (kind==='document' && isTextReadable...)). The capture path (materialize-preparation.ts:320 comment) now captures code whole with no secret/.env/authorization gate present in the file. This is the construction-leads/authorization-lags asymmetry on the capture axis specifically.
candidate_roots.finding_coverage: The #21 safety tail and provenance churn: R2-1 resume parity, R2-3 capture-vs-sample, R3-3 'label code as code', R5-2 e2e label rename, and the still-open round-7 materialize-preparation.ts:330 secret-bearing .env whole-file capture (a brand-new class opening rather than the loop converging). Sharpens that 'code' classification has no single behavioral+security owner.

candidate_roots.root_cause: Several invariants were retrofitted as natural-language instructions to the assessment/final-output LLM (or onto the failure-shaped subset of inputs at a single stop gate) instead of as a deterministic runtime construction/gate/append that structurally fails. When the guarantee is a prompt string, no object fails — the provenance validator checks required-section bindings, not the semantic content the instruction demanded — so a reviewer can always construct the case where the LLM follows the letter while dropping the substance, forcing a migration from instruction→deterministic that itself proceeds stage-by-stage (prompt → stop-gate → deterministic append → but claim projection still free). The metadata-stub for an over-budget observation reintroduces the very label-blind LLM trust the original #1 fix was meant to remove.
candidate_roots.mechanism: Verified pattern: run.ts:4029 emits evidence_body_omitted_for_budget=true as metadata the assessor still sees as a projected item (round-7: LLM may mark answerable from metadata). The revision-proposal policy began as a prompt instruction + stop gate (b0f6b0f), then needed a deterministic appendFinalOutputUnresolvedRevisionSection (R6-2), then round-7 found target_id unsanitized LLM text and that continuation/claim-projection still publish actionable_ready because neither consumes revisionProposal (run.ts:1449); only reject/defer are counted (extend/rename/split proposed-only).
candidate_roots.finding_coverage: The #2 revision-proposal chain (b0f6b0f stop-gate → R6-2 deterministic section → R7 sanitize target_id + carry blockers into claim projection + adversarial extend/rename/split), plus the label-blind-trust face of #1 (86324da answer_status judged blind to source → R7 stub re-introduces metadata-only answerability). A symptom-class that sharpens the deeper LLM-trust-vs-deterministic-enforcement distinction.

verdict.deeper_root_if_symptom: No-derived-expected-shape validation: every build/validate/project stage operates on the artifact INSTANCE in front of it (the present rows, the proposals it happens to hold, the value as copied) instead of deriving the required/expected shape ONCE from a single authority and asserting equality. "Mirroring" is the symptom: because there is no shared derived projection that both the builder emits and the validator re-derives, each disk-replay stage must hand-author its own copy of a carry-forward check or budget predicate, and the rounds simply walk one un-mirrored stage further each pass. The code shows the authority is literally present and unused: selected.adequacy_frame.required_elements is iterated to BUILD baseline rows (maturation-validation.ts:525, :652) but validateMaturationBaseline (:716) and validateActionabilityMatrix (:1003) only iterate the rows that EXIST (duplicate/enum/ref checks), never reconstruct the expected tuple set from required_elements and require exact one-to-one coverage. Same for the budget cluster: there is one true constraint (PROMPT_CHAR_LIMIT=50_000, run.ts:778) but no single function projects "what fits"; instead three independently-tuned proxies (EVIDENCE_EXCERPT_LIMIT 4_000, EVIDENCE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT 50, EVIDENCE_TOTAL_BUDGET_CHARS 24_000) each approximate it, and each round discovers one proxy that does not actually bound the real serialized payload. Same for eligibility: isFullExcerptProjectionEligible (run.ts:5700) and the capture-side predicate in materialize-preparation.ts:326-328 are two hand-copies of ONE rule (the materialize comment literally says "see isFullExcerptProjectionEligible in run.ts") that must agree but are not derived from a shared definition.
verdict.findings_explained: CLUSTER #22 candidate_limitation_refs carry-forward (8 findings) — all explained by the deeper root and by mirroring: maturation-validation.ts:670-681 baseline-vs-candidate (R2-2/R6 commit 7923f02,e88c119), :980-993 matrix-vs-baseline (F4 87cd9b8 / R2-5), :3911-3919 decision-actionable_ready-vs-matrix (R2-5/R3-1), :3924-3935 decision.limitation_refs-must-include-matrix-candidate-limit (R3-1 / round-5 corpus:286), :537/:790-799 mixed-lineage row-scope flip-flop (F2 revert -> R3-2 limitation_backed-gated restore, corpus:288), :3937-3945 + corpus:312/324 final-requestion convergence limitation must survive (R6-3 c61cc22), :3720 builder branch. Each was the same value re-asserted one stage downstream per round. CLUSTER #1 evidence-budget (7 findings) — run.ts:778/782/789/792 proxy constants, boundEvidenceBySerializedSize :4039, boundSingleEvidenceItem :4020: F1 reuse-hash rotation (87cd9b8), F3/R2-4/R3 question+domain-semantic evidence refs left content-blind (86324da, corpus:262/276), R4 count-cap insufficient because structural_data unbounded (1f4b2da), R5 serialized-size proxy (07dcdef, corpus:298), R6 lone-item-still-overflows stub (c61cc22, corpus:307), R6 stub-counted-as-projected honesty (corpus:328). Every round found a different proxy that did not actually enforce the one 50K cap. CLUSTER #21 full-excerpt/truncation eligibility (4 findings) — the two-copy predicate: a464732 introduces isFullExcerptProjectionEligible, R2-3 capture-side must match (materialize :327, corpus:274), R2-1/R5-2 resume fallback must mirror it (run.ts:5831, corpus:268), R3-3 label/event wording must follow the same kind (corpus:292/337). One eligibility rule re-threaded into capture, projection, resume, and label sinks.
verdict.structural_remediation: Replace per-stage instance-checking with derived-shape contracts so the property exists in exactly one place and every stage asserts equality against it. Concretely in this codebase: (A) candidate_limitation cluster — introduce one pure projection deriveLimitationCarryForward(selectedCandidate) -> {candidate_limitation_refs, expected_decision_limitation_refs} in maturation-validation.ts, have buildMaturationBaselineArtifact/buildActionabilityMatrixArtifact/buildMaturationContinuationDecisionArtifact all EMIT from it, and replace the four hand-written Set comparisons (:670, :982, :3911, :3924) with a single assertDerivedEquals(artifact.field, derived) helper; then the carry-forward chain collapses to one definition and no future stage can drift. (B) row-completeness (the P1 residual) — derive the expected (element×surface×dimension) tuple set from selected.adequacy_frame.required_elements (already computed at :652) into expectedBaselineRowIds, and make validateMaturationBaseline/validateActionabilityMatrix/validateMaturationContinuationDecision assert exact set equality (missing/extra/duplicate) against it instead of iterating present rows — this kills the deletion class that mirroring cannot. (C) evidence budget — collapse the three proxy constants into one boundForPromptBudget(items, PROMPT_CHAR_LIMIT - reserve) that measures the ACTUAL serialized observationPromptPayload (the thing the cap governs) and returns kept+stub+omitted counts; delete EVIDENCE_EXCERPT/CANDIDATE/TOTAL as independent tuning knobs (or make them derived caps inside that one function), so there is one place that can be wrong and it is measured against the real payload. (D) full-excerpt eligibility — move isFullExcerptProjectionEligible (and isTextReadableDocumentExtension) into a shared module imported by BOTH run.ts and materialize-preparation.ts, deleting the hand-copied predicate at materialize-preparation.ts:326-328 and the resume re-thread at :5831; capture-whole and project-whole then cannot disagree by construction. (E) revision-proposal disclosure — define ONE isUnappliedProposal(p) (covering all non-reuse actions, not just reject|defer) and one assembleUnresolvedProposalsSection used by the stop gate (:1443), policy (:4267), final-output append (:9822), and claim projection blocker, with target_id resolved/escaped once at the boundary. (F) governance: add the new prompt-contract/registry obligations in .onto/processes/reconstruct/reconstruct-contract-registry.yaml so these derived shapes are declared, and extend the existing G-series invariant-drift guard to assert that runtime budget/eligibility constants are derived-or-drift-tested against the contract, turning "a stage forgot to mirror" into a CI failure rather than a review round.

They are the value-preservation instances of the same deeper root (the candidate root names only the missing-ROW instance), which is why they kept recurring round after round in the identical patch shape.

CORROBORATING COUNTER-TEST (strengthens the root): maturation-validation.ts:1242-1251 (frontier validator) DOES implement a conservation check — it derives materialFrontierBaselineRows from the matrix and asserts every one projects to a question (coveredBaselineRows). This proves the team knows the derive-expected-set-and-diff pattern, but applied it (a) ad hoc at exactly ONE stage and (b) conserving against the MATRIX (an already-possibly-corrupted intermediate), not against the root authority required_elements. So an upstream-deleted blocker row never becomes a matrix frontier row and this existing check cannot catch it — exactly the candidate root's 'conservation against AUTHORITY, not against a present intermediate' thesis.

Pure concept/registry/test-hygiene findings — NOT this root (concept-economy axis):

These are 'declared-but-not-owned-by-registry' (the contract-runtime gap axis), not completeness-against-authority.

Net: of the ~24 distinct findings, the root DIRECTLY owns 3 (the entire P1 set) and is the deeper sibling of ~8 more (#22 value-drift). The remaining ~13 belong to two clearly independent axes (evidence-payload economics #1, truncation-provenance #21) plus concept/registry/test hygiene. So this root explains roughly 11/24 and is decisively NOT a universal explanation of the round-after-round loop — about half the recurrence is a separate prompt-budget axis.
verdict.deeper_root_if_symptom: The candidate root is genuine but stated one notch too narrow. The deeper structural root that subsumes BOTH the missing-row P1 trio AND the candidate_limitation #22 cluster is: 'reconstruct validators verify that records PRESENT in a projected artifact resolve and are internally consistent, but no stage derives the CLOSED expected projection from the immediately-upstream AUTHORITY artifact and asserts a conservation contract (no dropped/added/duplicated members AND no silently-mutated carried values) at each artifact hop.' Missing-rows (candidate root) and dropped-limitation-values (#22) are the two instances of this one absent invariant. Evidence proving this is the deeper root: (a) the frontier validator already conserves against the matrix but not against required_elements — conservation is applied ad hoc, not as a uniform hop invariant; (b) every #22 fix and the requested P1 fixes share the identical patch shape (derive expected set/value from upstream, Set-diff, fail on mismatch), just at different fields/hops, which is exactly why the reviewer can construct a new dual each round. The loop converges only when conservation becomes a single derive-expected-from-upstream-authority-and-diff mechanism applied uniformly across baseline->matrix->frontier->continuation->claim, rather than re-derived per field per round.
verdict.structural_remediation:
Introduce ONE generic projection-conservation invariant in maturation-validation.ts and apply it at every artifact hop, replacing the per-field/per-round Set checks:

1) Authority-anchored expected-set derivation. Add a helper `deriveExpectedBaselineTuples(selected)` that enumerates the closed cartesian set of (purpose_element_ref x actionability_surface_ref x maturity_dimension_ref) from selected.adequacy_frame.required_elements (the same required_elements already loaded at maturation-validation.ts:651). In validateMaturationBaseline (:716 loop), after the present-row pass, diff baseline.baseline_rows against this expected set: emit missing_required_coverage for any expected tuple absent (this is the existing failure kind — reuse it, no new vocabulary), and require deterministic tuple ids so add/drop/dup are all caught. This closes :716.

2) Generic hop-conservation helper `assertProjectionConservation({upstreamIds, downstreamRefs, requireOneToOne, label})` returning violations (missing/extra/duplicate). Reuse it at:
   - validateActionabilityMatrix (:1003): upstream = baseline.baseline_rows ids, require one matrix row per baseline row with deterministic matrix-${slug(baseline_row_id)} ids. Closes :1003.
   - validateMaturationContinuationDecision (:3885): recompute expected included/excluded partition from actionabilityMatrix.rows (closed rows -> included, non-closed -> excluded or blocking) and require claim_scope to equal it; additionally require all matrix ROW-level limitation_refs (not just candidate-level) to survive into decision.limitation_refs. Closes :3885.
   - Refactor the existing frontier check (:1242-1251 materialFrontierBaselineRows) to call the same helper, AND additionally feed the authority-derived expected set so a row dropped upstream is caught even though it never became a matrix frontier row.

3) Fold the #22 value-conservation into the same mechanism. The candidate_limitation_refs Set-equality checks at :669-683, :982-995, :3920-3936 are ad-hoc instances of value-preservation; express them through a `assertCarriedValueConserved({upstream, downstream, field})` so the convergence-limitation and final-requestion-limitation refs (and any future carried field) are covered by one rule instead of a new branch each round. This is what stops the round-after-round recurrence for cluster #22.

4) Drift guard so the invariant is not silently bypassed later: add a unit test that, for each hop, constructs the dual (delete one expected member; mutate one carried value) and asserts the conservation violation fires — making the omission class a tested contract rather than something a future edit can quietly weaken.

Scope note: this remediation does NOT touch the two independent axes (evidence-payload budgeting in run.ts:4039+, truncation-provenance in run.ts:5700/materialize-preparation.ts) — those need their own fixes and are out of this class.

verdict.counterevidence:
The root does NOT explain the two LARGEST clusters, which together are ~16 of the 24 findings:

(A) LIMITATION-PROPAGATION DRIFT cluster (~10): R3-1, R3-2, R2-2, R2-5, F4, and maturation-validation.ts:851/982/3745/3912/537/3755, plus R6-3. These recur not because a contract lagged runtime, but because the source-level limitation must survive FOUR hops (selected.candidate.limitation_refs -> baseline.candidate_limitation_refs -> matrix.candidate_limitation_refs -> continuation.decision.limitation_refs -> public claim), and each round Codex finds the NEXT unguarded hop. The fix is always 'add a validator proving the value did not silently drop at this hop' — a missing-invariant problem, not a declared-vs-wired problem. Bumping/syncing a contract sha would not have caught any of these.

(B) EVIDENCE-CONTENT-vs-BUDGET cluster (~6): #1 R2-4, F3, R4-1, R5-1, R6-1, run.ts:4080, run.ts:4029. These recur because each round a new way for evidence bodies to NOT reach the assessor was found (count cap vs serialized size vs structural_data vs batching unsplittable single question vs stub-counted-as-projected). Pure runtime budgeting bugs; no contract surface involved.

(C) The adversarial P1s (maturation-validation.ts:716/1003/3885) — the deepest findings — are 'validate present rows, never derive the required tuple set from required_elements.' verdict.deeper_root_if_symptom: The deeper root is: VALIDATORS CHECK LOCAL WELL-FORMEDNESS OF EACH ARTIFACT IN ISOLATION RATHER THAN BEING DERIVED FROM A SINGLE UPSTREAM SOURCE-OF-TRUTH AND PROVING CONSERVATION ACROSS HOPS. Every artifact in the reconstruct chain (seed projection contract, maturation baseline, actionability matrix, continuation decision, claim, source-evidence projection) is independently authored/serialized, and its validator only checks that what is present is internally consistent. There is no mechanism that (a) DERIVES the expected shape/values/row-set of a downstream artifact from its upstream authority, and (b) FAILS when a required element/value/limitation/contract-field is absent rather than merely malformed. 'Contracts lag runtime' (the candidate) is one face of this: the contract surface is a SEPARATE artifact that isn't derived from runtime, so it drifts. But the limitation-drift cluster is the SAME disease on the value axis (no conserved-quantity check across baseline->matrix->continuation->claim), the evidence cluster is the SAME disease on the budget axis (no end-to-end 'cited evidence body actually reaches the assessor' assertion), and the adversarial P1s are the SAME disease on the row-set axis (validate-present-not-derived-required). Codex is essentially fuzzing the chain hop-by-hop and finding one unguarded boundary per round. The candidate names the declared-surface manifestation; the deeper root is the absence of derive-from-upstream + conservation-across-hops validation as a structural pattern.
verdict.structural_remediation:
Concrete, class-level remediation in THIS codebase (maturation-validation.ts + run.ts), three structural mechanisms instead of per-hop patches:

1. DERIVE-EXPECTED-THEN-DIFF for every chained validator. In maturation-validation.ts, refactor validateMaturationBaseline / validateActionabilityMatrix / validateMaturationContinuationDecision to take their UPSTREAM artifact and compute the expected element set deterministically: baseline rows MUST equal the tuple set derived from selected.adequacy_frame.required_elements x surfaces x dimensions (kills P1 :716); matrix rows MUST be a bijection with baseline_rows via deterministic matrix-${slug(baseline_row_id)} ids (kills P1 :1003); continuation included/excluded refs MUST be recomputed from actionabilityMatrix.rows (kills P1 :3885). The validator FAILS on missing/extra, not just malformed.

2. A CONSERVED-QUANTITY assertion for limitation_refs across the chain. Introduce one helper, e.g. assertLimitationConservation(upstream, downstream, fieldPath), and call it at each hop so candidate_limitation_refs and convergence/final-requestion limitation refs are proven to be a superset/equal at baseline->matrix->continuation->claim in ONE place. This collapses the ~10 limitation-drift findings (851/982/3745/3912/537/3755/R6-3) into a single invariant instead of six hand-written validators that each Codex round discovers is missing.

3. DERIVE THE CONTRACT SHA FROM A SINGLE OWNED SHAPE, and add a drift gate. Every silent-defect fix in this PR widened one producer surface — whole-file capture (#21), cited evidence bodies (#1), candidate/convergence limitation refs (#22), unapplied revision proposals (#2) — and the new surface's invariant is then re-checked independently at N downstream sites (capture site, projection gate, truncation sink, resume fallback, e2e consumer / baseline, matrix, continuation, claim-projection / stop-gate, disclosure, sanitizer). verdict.structural_remediation:

2) For the propagation axis (#22) and gate axis (#2) — replace per-stage independent re-checks with a single derive-and-assert invariant. In maturation-validation.ts, derive the expected limitation-ref set ONCE from the selected purpose candidate and require every downstream artifact (baseline.candidate_limitation_refs, matrix, continuation decision.limitation_refs, claim_scope) to equal that derived set via one shared assertEqualRefSet helper, rather than the current chain of pairwise drift checks (:670, :980, :3745...). Likewise derive the expected baseline row-tuple set from selected.adequacy_frame.required_elements and require exact 1:1 coverage at baseline/matrix/continuation (kills the missing-row P1 findings :716/:1003/:3885 as a class). The common discipline: when a fix widens a producer surface, the new invariant must be owned by ONE deterministic derive-and-assert function that every consumer calls, instead of being re-stated as an inline predicate at each site.

verdict.deeper_root_if_symptom: consumed-on-trust-not-rederived-from-authority: every consuming stage trusts a value/structure HANDED to it by an upstream producer — LLM prose, a copied artifact field, or an author-produced set — and checks it (if at all) pointwise where the author happened to think of it, instead of RE-DERIVING/RE-CONSTRUCTING it deterministically from the single source of authority at the point of consumption. "Delegated to LLM prose" is merely the most extreme carrier (free text) of this disease; the dominant recurrence is structured carriers (candidate_limitation_refs copied candidate->baseline->matrix->continuation->claim with a per-hop equality check added one hop per round) and author-produced sets trusted whole (validateMaturationBaseline validates only PRESENT rows, validateActionabilityMatrix does not require 1:1 baseline coverage — the row SET is trusted, not derived from selected.adequacy_frame.required_elements). A co-equal sibling root drives the rename/budget/resume cluster: incomplete-change-propagation-across-mirrors (one path/consumer/contract changed, its mirror/sibling/.onto-contract/E2E-consumer not). Candidate root is one narrow face of consumed-on-trust.

synthesis.deepest_root: consumed-on-trust-not-rederived-from-authority (with conservation-across-hops). Every reconstruct stage TRUSTS the artifact instance handed to it by an upstream producer — an author-produced row set, a copied field value, an LLM prose answer, a contract surface, a budget proxy — and at most checks that what is PRESENT is internally consistent and resolves. No stage DERIVES the closed expected shape/value/row-set ONCE from the single upstream authority (selected.adequacy_frame.required_elements, the selected purpose candidate, the 50K PROMPT_CHAR_LIMIT, the one eligibility rule) and asserts equality/conservation at the point of consumption. Because the guarantee lives nowhere as a single derived contract, it is hand-re-asserted at each disk-replay stage; every Codex round constructs the dual at the next un-guarded hop (delete a required row, drop a carried limitation ref, find a budget proxy that doesn't bound the real payload, find a consumer that didn't get the eligibility memo), and the number of rounds is bounded by chain length, not by the correctness of any single fix. VERIFIED IN CODE: validateMaturationBaseline (maturation-validation.ts:716) iterates only baseline.baseline_rows after a length>0 guard (709), reading required_elements (652) for forward resolution only — never reconstructing and diffing the expected tuple set, so deleting a blocker/high row passes every guard and silently erases scope. The team already knows the derive-and-conserve pattern (materialFrontierBaselineRows/coveredBaselineRows, :1155/:1242) but applied it ad hoc against the MATRIX (a possibly-already-corrupted intermediate), not against the root authority. The 50K cap (run.ts:778) is the one true constraint yet is approximated by three independently-tuned proxies (EXCERPT 4_000 :782, TOTAL 24_000 :789, CANDIDATE 50 :792). isFullExcerptProjectionEligible (run.ts:5700) is hand-re-threaded at :5724/:5831/:5882 and re-copied in materialize-preparation.ts:328 whose comment literally points back to run.ts.

This subsumes candidate #2 (the missing-ROW instance) plus the entire #22 limitation-ref cluster (the value-drift instance). synthesis.recommendation:
Stop patching per-stage and install the missing invariant as structure. The 7-round pattern is not bad luck or shallow fixes — it is structurally guaranteed. All four adversarial verdicts converge: the reconstruct chain (baseline -> matrix -> frontier -> continuation -> claim, plus the assessment-prompt and capture/projection paths) has NO single derived authority for its load-bearing properties. Each property — required row coverage, carried limitation refs, the 50K prompt budget, whole-file eligibility, unresolved-proposal disclosure — exists only as a SET of hand-authored re-assertions, one per disk-replay stage, with nothing deriving them from one source. So every Codex fix hardens exactly the stage named, and the reviewer constructs the dual at the next un-guarded hop. The round count is bounded by chain length, not by fix quality; continued patching will run until the chain is exhausted, and meanwhile the three highest-severity P1 findings (delete-a-required-row erases blocker scope; matrix drops a baseline row; claim_scope omits non-closed rows and the public claim preserves the lie) remain UNADDRESSED after all 7 rounds because no round attempted the one thing that catches them: derive the expected set from authority and diff.

Concrete plan to break the cycle:
1. Land the rank-1 conservation mechanism (deriveExpected + assertProjectionConservation + assertCarriedValueConserved, reusing the existing missing_required_coverage failure kind) and apply it at every hop. This single mechanism closes the entire P1 trio AND collapses the #22 cluster that drove most rounds — converting a per-round patch into one invariant. The team already has the pattern in-repo (the frontier validator at :1155/:1242); generalize it and re-anchor it to required_elements instead of the matrix.
2. In the SAME PR, close the three independent axes the conservation fix does not touch, each as a single-owner fix: collapse the three budget proxies into one boundForPromptBudget measuring the real serialized payload and treat the over-budget stub as omitted (rank-2); close the .env/secret whole-file capture data-exposure hole introduced by this PR's code-expansion via a sensitivity-gated (not kind-gated) authorization (rank-3); route all non-reuse revision proposals through one isUnappliedProposal predicate consumed by the stop gate, the disclosure append, AND claim projection (rank-4).
3. Add dual-case drift tests for each invariant (delete a member, mutate a carried value, over-budget item, secret-bearing ref, unresolved extend/rename/split proposal) so the omission/exposure classes become tested contracts a future edit fails on — not something a later stage can quietly drop. Replace the vacuous shape-only CLI tests with these behavior assertions.
4. Governance to stop regeneration: promote the new concepts (candidate_limitation_refs carry-forward, source_evidence_projection, evidence_body_omitted_for_budget, unresolved_revision_proposals) into .onto/processes/reconstruct/reconstruct-contract-registry.yaml with their match/carry/claim obligations, and extend the existing G-series invariant-drift guard so runtime budget/eligibility constants are derived-or-drift-tested against the contract. This turns "a stage forgot to mirror" and "a contract lagged runtime" into a CI failure instead of a review round (closing the contracts-lag cluster as a class). The competency-question assessment contract sha should be BUILT from the declared shape so any new prompt-surface field auto-rotates it.

Net: four single-owner derive-and-assert mechanisms plus a drift gate replace ~20 per-hop patches. After this, a round-8 reviewer cannot construct a new dual by walking one stage further, because the property lives in exactly one place and every stage asserts equality against it. Do NOT ship another round of stage-local patches — the P1s prove that approach has already failed to reach the load-bearing gaps after 7 attempts.
